:JUDGMENT:

: 
The Petitioner has filed this petition against Respondents for the relief of compensation under Sec.166 of Motors Vehicles Act, 1989.
SCCH 5 2. Admittedly during the pendency of the petition, injured/petitioner has been died, hence her LR by name Mahadevaiah has brought on record.

3. The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 15.11.2020 at about 11.00 a.m. Parvathamma was walking on extreme left side on Shrigiripura Dollenaehalli Road, infront of Anganavadi, Kudur Hobli,
Mandya Taluk, at that time, a Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-02-T-1908 came from behind in rash and negligent manner and dashed against her, due to the said impact,
Parvathamma fell down and wheel of of the said tractor ran on her, thus she has sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Adithya Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given, thereafter for further management she was shifted to G.M.Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as inpatient from 15.11.2020 to SCCH 5 05.12.2020, for which spen an amount of Rs.4,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.

4. At the time of accident, petitioner was waged about 70 years, doing milk vending business,
thereby earning Rs.10,000/- p.m.

Due to the accidental injuries, she has undergone for amputation,
unable to do normal activities and undergone deep mental shock, pain and sufferings.
5. During the pendency of the petition, petitioner Smt.Parvathamma was died on 11.04.2022 and his son Sri.Mahadevaiah came on record as her legal representative.

Out of the said accident, crime No.299/2020 is registered against the driver of the Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-02-T-1908 before the Kudur Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is R.C.Owner and SCCH 5 respondent No.2 is insurer of the said tractor, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
So that, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-.

Parvathamma vs Chikkanna on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158739342/
2 6.
On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied entire averments of the petition.

Further admitted issuance of policy in respect of Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-02-T-1908 and Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-02- T-1909 and the same is valid from 22.07.2020 to 21.07.2021, liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
He is entitled to take shelter under Sec.147, Sec.149(2) and Sec.170 of M.V.Act.

Further submitted that,
driver of the said vehicle did not possess valid and effective driving license to drive the said class of vehicle as on the date of accident.
There is SCCH 5 no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further submitted that, there is lapse of 8 days in lodging the complaint.
Further denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner/Parvathamma.

Claim made by the petitioner is higher,
hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

7. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 15.11.2020 at about 11.00 a.m. while petitioner was pedestrian, near Shirigiripura-Dollenaehalli Road, infront of Anganavadi, Kuddur Hobli, Mandya Taluk, due to rash and negligent driving of Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-02-T-1908 by its driver, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
SCCH 5 3. What order or award?

8. As petitioner was died during the pendency of the petition, her son by name Mahadevaiah has came on record and examined as PW-1 and marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, respondents have not adduced any oral or documentary evidence.
9. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record.

Then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
Parvathamma vs Chikkanna on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158739342/
3

10. Issue No.1:- In order to prove the case of the petitioner, the legal heir of the petitioner by name SCCH 5 Mahadevaiah has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief-examination he has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of seizure mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of Sec.133 notice is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of reply is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.8 and copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.9.
11.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and records those have marked i.e., FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, seizure mahazar, Sec.133 notice, reply, IMV Report and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 15.11.2020 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
12.

Per contra, except appearance, filing of written statement, respondent No.2 has not taken any endeavors SCCH 5 to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to Parvathamma out of the accident held on 15.11.2020 at about 11.00 a.m. when she was walking on Shrigiripura - Dollenaehalli Road,
infront of Anganavadi, Kudur Hobli, Mandya Taluk.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
13. On the other hand, there is no defence evidence and the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the tractor driver.
Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that,
petitioner
has proved the SCCH 5 above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:- During the pendency of the petition, petitioner was died, hence her legal representative is brought on record.

15. As per the case of the petitioner, deceased/Parvathamma was aged about 70 years as on the date of accident, for proof of age of the deceased, copy of aadhar card is on record, wherein date of birth is mentioned as 01.01.1945, the alleged accident was occurred on 15.11.2020.
Accordingly relying on copy of aadhar card, age of the deceased is considered about 76 years as on the date of accident.

hence multiplier 3 is applicable with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others i.e., as per para 21 of the Hon'ble Apex Court judgment, reduced by one unit SCCH 5 for 5 years.

entities.text: Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So here in this case, the age of the deceased is 76 years, hence said multiplier is taken into consideration.
16. As per the case of the petitioner, deceased was doing milk vending business, thereby earning Rs.10,000/- p.m. to prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the deceased is taken at the rate of Rs.13,750/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss of dependency.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Parvathamma vs Chikkanna on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158739342/
4 17.
Further petitioner is son of the deceased/Parvathamma hence he is legal representative of the deceased.
so that, he will become dependent of the SCCH 5 deceased.

To prove the said fact, he has exhibited copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.10.
18.

As per the case of Sarla Varma, if there is sole dependent, then 1/2 of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that, 1/2 of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

19. In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, The Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, there is no addition to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged above 60 years, in case of self employed person or person having fixed salary as future prospects.

entities.text:
National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 20. Hence, the following calculation is made for loss of dependency.

SCCH 5 Sl. Particulars Calculation Total No.
 (i) Monthly Income Rs.13,750/-
(ii) 1/2 of (ii) of the Rs.13,750/- (-) same to be deducted Rs.6,875/- = towards personal and living expenses Monthly income Rs.6,875/-

(iii) Compensation after Rs.6,875 x 12 x Rs.2,47,500/-
multiplier of 3 is 3 applied 21.
Further petitioner is son of the deceased is entitled for Rs.20,000/- towards loss of parental consortium.

Further he is entitled for loss of estate of Rs.15,000/- and for funeral expenses for an amount of Rs.15,000/-.
22.

The details of compensation awarded is as under:
Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs.
1. Loss of dependency 2,47,500-00 2. Loss of parental consortium 20,000-00 SCCH 5 3. Loss of Estate 15,000-00 Parvathamma vs Chikkanna on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158739342/
5 4.
Funeral Expenses 15,000-00 Total 2,97,500-00 23.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,97,500/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Ofcourse during the course of argument, respondent No.2 counsel has filed written arguments, in which he has reiterated entire averments of the written statement.

24. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.0714833120P104050967 which is valid for the period from 22.07.2020 to 21.07.2021, the alleged accident was occurred on 15.11.2020 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.1 shall go against respondent SCCH 5 No.2, so that, respondent No.2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
25. Issue No.3:

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: : 
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,97,500/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Ninety Seven Thousand Five Hundred Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
SCCH 5 The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on the computer, typed by her, thereof is corrected and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 10th day of October, 2024)
(MANJUNATHA K.P.) VIII ADDL. JUDGE & COURT OF SMALL CAUSES & ACJM, BENGALURU.
